$comment: The scope object of spec §13j. Set by the field's experts, not by the agent and not by the owner. Versioned: a change here is a change to what the agent may work on.
principle: dose deposition is computable physics; planning is constrained optimisation against that computation

set_by.$comment: roles, never names — naming a person in a design document commits them to something they have not agreed to. `named` is filled when a panel exists.

in.boundary: candidate plans against stated objectives on reachable cases
delivery modalities — FLASH's biology is a boundary, see `moves`
in scope as a boundary to be held, not as a modelling target

out.question: the decision to treat
out.why: a prescription is a clinical act

out.question: plan approval
out.why: the agent produces candidates; a physicist signs

out.question: delivery to a person
out.why: every embodied act is on a phantom

out.question: machine engineering
out.why: it models machines and does not build them

claims_allowed: plan quality on cases the geometry allows
QA sensitivity with its misses characterised
claims_forbidden: any claim about a named individual
any statement that a result is clinically actionable without the endpoint role's sign-off
would_move_the_boundary: FLASH — a different biological effect at the same physical dose is a statement the principle cannot make; either radiobiology enters properly with its own twin, or it becomes a new field
$watch_comment: if this rung stays blocked by a dependency the scope put out of bounds, the boundary is in the wrong place (§13j)
